podcasts.title: Dario Amodei WARNS: You Have No Idea What's Coming In 18 Months
podcasts.description:
Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic and former OpenAI research chief, warns that AI could create a country of geniuses inside a data center within just one to five years, triggering unprecedented disruption to employment, national security and democracy. He explains how AI could eliminate entry-level jobs in software engineering, law, finance and consulting, potentially wiping out half of white-collar entry-level positions and pushing unemployment to 10–20%. He warns that autonomous drone swarms, mass surveillance and increasingly independent AI agents could undermine constitutional protections and human control. Amodei calls for international agreements to prevent AI-powered biological weapons and argues that controlling advanced AI is a complex engineering challenge, while admitting that dangerous failures are inevitable if development continues this quickly.

podcasts.title: AMD CEO Lisa Su: Are We in an AI Bubble? | TomorrowX Summit
podcasts.description:
"Are we in an AI bubble? AMD Chair and CEO Lisa Su says this is the most transformative technology of the last 50 years, and that what she's seeing doesn't look cyclical, it looks generational. She sits down with Dom Rizzo of T. Rowe Price on stage at TomorrowX Summit in her hometown of Austin.

Lisa looks back on the early bets that shaped AMD, from chiplets to high performance computing, and how AMD became a data center first company. She explains how she thinks about ROI on the AI infrastructure build-out, why "the noise will work itself out in time" amid the latest Nvidia headlines, and how AMD works with Washington on export controls so the world builds on the American AI stack.

She also shares how Anthropic got its model running on AMD over a weekend with Claude, why AI agents are driving a CPU comeback, the launch of Venice and the MI455 and Helios racks, and her hope that every family will have a story of how AI improved their lives.

KEY TAKEAWAYS
• AI is the most transformative technology of the last 50 years, and it makes sense to invest
• This cycle doesn't look cyclical, it looks generational
• Separate from the noise: the noise works itself out in time
• Export controls protect national security, while the world should build on the American AI stack
• Frontier models now help port software across hardware in days, not months
• Agents need orchestration, which makes CPUs critical again
• The right compute for the right workload: CPUs, GPUs, FPGAs and custom silicon

podcasts.description:

Brad set out to change that. When he first called me about Invest America in 2020, I thought it was a fool’s errand. Six years later, nearly 70 million children have accounts in their name, and every American newborn receives $1,000 in the S&P 500. The challenge now is getting families to claim their accounts, since free money is surprisingly hard to give away.

Brad and Geoffrey believe even a small nest egg, when given a head start on compounding, can help rebuild faith in capitalism. As AI reshapes the economy, they see these accounts as the basis of a new social contract built on ownership and participation, where every child owns a piece of the upside.

Since recording: the AP called Texas for Gina Hinojosa, who would pause datacenter permitting, and Georgia for Keisha Lance Bottoms, and Democrats took a 3-2 majority on Georgia’s Public Service Commission, which sets power rates. (As of Nov 4, 2:35 PM ET.)
